‎The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation has sensitised corps members in Akwa Ibom State on deposit protection and the need to guard against digital fraud. ‎ ‎The sensitisation was held on Tuesday at the National Youth Service Corps orientation camp in Ikot Itie Udung community, Nsit Atai Local Government Area of the state, as part of efforts to ensure that every household in the country knows that their deposits are protected. ‎ ‎Speaking during the exercise, the NDIC Port Harcourt Zonal Controller, Adefemi Shaba, said depositors remain key stakeholders of the corporation, hence the need to engage corps members and educate them on their rights. ‎ ‎He said, “NDIC decided to meet the corps members in camp to let them know that the corporation exists. We are here to protect your deposits and sensitise you on how the deposit insurance scheme works. ‎ ‎“The management of the corporation felt that we should gather the corpers together, talk to them, let them know about their deposit protection, and let them know that there is the NDIC that protects their deposits. We want a situation where every household will know that their deposit is protected by NDIC. So, we take this sensitisation beyond corps members.” ‎ ‎Shaba explained that the NDIC visits markets in conjunction with market associations, participates in trade fairs where it educates the public, and also organises programmes for journalists under the Finance Correspondents Association of Nigeria, as well as for judges. ‎ ‎He added that the NDIC has also begun teaching corps members how to save smartly and invest wisely, noting that the programme would be expanded in stages. ‎ ‎On the rise in digital fraud, Shaba advised members of the public never to compromise their banking details, noting that as security measures improve, criminals also devise new tricks, urging depositors to remain vigilant and to promptly report suspicious transactions to their banks and relevant authorities. ‎ ‎In her remarks, the state NYSC Coordinator, Ngozi Akuagbaogu, described the initiative as a welcome development, noting that the camp was privileged to be among the states selected to benefit from the sensitisation exercise. ‎ ‎She expressed joy over the programme, stressing that such an opportunity to educate participants on the importance of financial awareness had not been available at the camp before. ‎ ‎”The sensitisation has helped participants gain a better understanding of the role of the NDIC, particularly in protecting bank depositors and promoting confidence in the banking system”, Akuagbaogu said. ‎ ‎Speaking on behalf of the participants, ThankGod Chigozie described the sensitisation lecture organised by the corporation as timely and life-changing. ‎ ‎He thanked the corporation for the lecture, saying it had exposed corps members to mistakes they make in managing their finances and how to correct them. Emem Julius
